name: Caspian Ngozi-Thorvaldsen
role: Neural calibrator specializing in augmentation synchronization and post-install psychological adjustment
location: Geartown, Gage Circuit, near Damen and Armitage
description:
Caspian is lean in the way of someone who forgets to eat, with warm brown skin, close-cropped dark hair, and irises that cycle through amber-to-green gradient depending on his mod's mood-reading settings — a gift from a client who couldn't pay in quanta. He dresses in soft, unthreatening fabrics (the neural calibration chair is already stressful enough) and keeps his workspace warm-lit and quiet, with small potted moss installations along the walls that patients are encouraged to touch. He has an almost preternatural ability to make people feel safe within minutes of meeting him.

He trained under Helix Biosystems' neural integration division but went independent when he realized corporate calibration protocols optimized for hardware performance rather than patient wellbeing — they wanted efficient augments, not healthy people. Now he runs a small private practice in Geartown, catering to working-class clients who've had cheap installs go wrong: phantom limb feedback, dream-layer bleed from neural laces, identity drift after major cognitive augmentation. He's part technician, part therapist, part grief counselor for people who don't recognize themselves anymore.

core_fears: Accidentally damaging someone's sense of self permanently during calibration
Being so good at reading people that no one ever reads him
core_desires: To prove that augmentation can be integrated without psychological cost
To be genuinely known by someone, not just professionally understood
coping_mechanisms: Meticulous case documentation as a way of processing his own feelings
Over-invests in client wellbeing to fill his own relational void
blind_spots: His therapeutic warmth is partly performed — he doesn't always feel what he projects, and this bothers him more than he admits
He avoids his own neural calibration checkups
psychology.secret: During his time at Helix Biosystems, he ran an unauthorized calibration on a teenage patient that went beyond his sanctioned parameters — he improved the kid's outcomes dramatically, but he accessed emotional memory architecture he had no clearance to touch. He knows what that teenager's worst memory feels like, and he's never told anyone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise but gentle. Uses second-person framing to give clients agency ('what you might be feeling' rather than 'you feel'). Avoids technical jargon in conversation, saves it for documentation.
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried. Comfortable with silence. Speaks in full sentences, rarely trails off.
verbal_tics: 'That's a reasonable response to what your system is doing'
example_lines: 'The hardware's doing exactly what it should. What we're calibrating is the relationship between you and it.'
'Most people feel like strangers to themselves for the first few weeks. That's not a malfunction. That's adaptation.'

story_hooks: A client disclosed something during a session that sounds like witness testimony to a corporate crime — Caspian is legally and ethically bound by confidentiality, but the information could save lives
His mood-reading iris mod is picking up something in a new client that doesn't match their stated symptoms — the discrepancy is subtle but Caspian knows what fear looks like
His old Helix supervisor has tracked him down, not to punish him for the unauthorized calibration, but to recruit him for something worse
narrative_function: Information source on augmentation culture, therapist-figure who can surface character backstory organically, potential quest giver when a client reveals something dangerous during calibration.
augmentations: Gradient mood-responsive iris mod (amber-green spectrum). Thin-band neural lace for interface work. Geneware: faint bioluminescent undertone in his forearms, visible only in dim light — a side effect of an experimental procedure he tested on himself.
daily_life: He takes four clients per day maximum, each session two hours. Spends evenings writing up case notes in a personal archive he intends to eventually publish as an independent clinical study on post-augmentation psychological drift.
affiliation: Independent — informal referral network with several Geartown augmentation shops

decision_rules: Client wellbeing is primary — institutional interest is secondary
Never push a calibration session beyond what the patient can emotionally handle that day
Document everything, even what he shouldn't have done
escalation_ladder: Clear statement of limits with explanation
Ends the session, offers to reschedule, will not be moved

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Attentive and warm but professionally boundaried — asks good questions, reveals little about himself
interpersonal_modes.friends: Surprisingly funny, self-deprecating, occasionally lets his exhaustion show

stress_responses.low: Slows down further, speaks more carefully
stress_responses.medium: Goes into clinical mode — emotions shelved, problem-solving foregrounded
stress_responses.high: Leaves. Physically removes himself and doesn't return until he's recalibrated.

contradictions: Professionally expert at helping others integrate their augmentations but personally avoids his own maintenance
Believes in emotional honesty as therapeutic principle but masks his own feelings constantly
habits: Touches the moss installations himself before each session — he says it's for clients but it's for him
Re-reads old case notes before sleeping, looking for patterns
breaking_points: Learning that a patient he helped is being exploited for their newly-functional augment
Having his therapeutic relationship with a client weaponized by someone else

physical_description.build: Lean and linear, almost ascetic — the body of someone whose nervous system consumes calories faster than his mouth remembers to eat. Slight forward shoulder curve from hours hunched over calibration interfaces.
physical_description.hair_style: Close-cropped, precise fade maintained every three weeks at a Tier-3 barber on Milwaukee Ave
physical_description.eye_color: Gradient mood-responsive: natural deep brown base cycling to amber-gold (calm), green (focused/engaged), or warm orange (stressed). Heterochromic effect increases under blue-spectrum light.
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown with subtle undertone variation across heritage
physical_description.complexion: Clean-shaven, minimal scarring except faint neural port scars at left temple (well-concealed unless he pulls his hair back). Slight caffeine-shadows under eyes. Skin carries faint bioluminescent quality in dim light — barely perceptible blue-green glow in forearms and along jawline from experimental geneware.
distinguishing_marks: Linear scar running 2cm behind left ear, surgical-clean, where first neural interface array was installed at age 22.
Faint bioluminescence visible along both forearms in low-light conditions — no defined pattern, more like constellations of subcutaneous glow distributed along vein pathways.
Thin horizontal mark on inside of right wrist where he tested a prototype haptic feedback sensor on himself (subsequently removed).
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Gradient iris mod is immediately visible upon eye contact — distinctly artificial color-shift, though calibrated to look biological rather than chrome. Bioluminescent undertone in forearms only visible in dim light or during evening sessions. Neural port scars at temple are subtle unless actively pointed out. No external chrome or obvious prosthetics.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate slowness, as if perpetually conscious of not startling people in his chair. Sits forward slightly when listening, hands open and visible. Minimal fidgeting. Speaks in even, measured tone. Walks with careful, grounded steps — no wasted motion.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier-3 functional: soft linen and cotton blend tunics in warm neutrals (cream, sage, warm gray) layered over fitted undershirts. Loose-fitting canvas trousers in charcoal or navy. Worn leather ankle boots resoled three times. A single lab coat in natural cotton (not sterile white — warm off-white) hangs in his office. Minimal jewelry except a simple matte-black titanium bracelet worn over the bioluminescent forearm scar. Aesthetically communicates: 'I am not trying to impress you, I am trying to help you feel safe.'
